definitions.explanation: To forcefully push someone or something away from oneself.
To push with enough force to make someone fall or stagger.

examples.japanese: {相手|あいて}を{突|つ}き{飛|と}ばす。
{彼|かれ}は{邪魔者|じゃまもの}を{突|つ}き{飛|と}ばして{逃|に}げた。
examples.english: He pushed the person blocking his way aside and ran away.

examples.japanese: {怒|いか}りで{彼女|かのじょ}を{突|つ}き{飛|と}ばしてしまった。
examples.english: I ended up shoving her in anger.

notes:
COMPOUND VERB:
{突|つ}く (to thrust, to poke) + {飛|と}ばす (to make fly, to send away)

TRANSITIVITY:
{他動詞|たどうし} (transitive) - takes を to mark the person/thing being pushed

ASPECT ({ている}):
{突|つ}き{飛|と}ばしている indicates the action is in progress.

REGISTER:
Neutral. Can be used in both casual and formal contexts.

RELATED COMPOUND VERBS:
- {突|つ}き{刺|さ}す: to stab
- {蹴|け}り{飛|と}ばす: to kick away
- {殴|なぐ}り{倒|たお}す: to knock down with a punch

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人|ひと}を{突|つ}き{飛|と}ばす: to push a person away
- {力|ちから}いっぱい{突|つ}き{飛|と}ばす: to shove with all one's strength
